pricing.title: Pricing & Engagement Models
pricing.subtitle: How we scope and price serious software engagements -- transparently, without a one-size-fits-all price tag.
pricing.philosophyBody: Custom software isn't a commodity, so we don't pretend it has a single sticker price. We scope each engagement around your real operational problem, then agree a fixed structure before any build work starts.
pricing.modelsSubtitle: Different problems call for different shapes of engagement. Most projects start with one of these.
pricing.costDriversBody: Scope, user and permission complexity, integrations, AI requirements, data migration, and delivery speed are the main factors. The estimator below reflects all of them.
pricing.paymentBody: Payment structure is agreed per engagement during scoping. We work in clear milestones so you always know what's being delivered and when.
pricing.ownershipBody: Ownership terms are confirmed in the engagement agreement. We're happy to discuss them upfront -- there are no surprises at handover.
pricing.supportBody: Post-launch support is offered as a separate, optional plan rather than bundled into the build, so you only pay for what you need.

meta.title: CRMA — AI-Native CRM · Engineering capability showcase
meta.description: An engineering capability showcase from HexaTerminal: a multi-tenant CRM and sales operations platform with deterministic pipeline logic, graph-defined workflows and AI actions that wait for human approval. Seeded demonstration data.

teaser.title: CRMA
teaser.subtitle: AI-Native CRM & Sales Operations Platform
teaser.body: A multi-tenant CRM architecture combining sales operations, workflow automation, deterministic pipeline intelligence and governed AI actions.
teaser.disclosure: Engineering capability showcase · seeded demonstration data

hero.title: CRMA — AI-Native CRM
hero.lead: A multi-tenant CRM and sales operations platform designed around controlled workflows, deterministic business rules and AI actions that require explicit human review before consequential changes.
hero.stack: Laravel 12 · React 19 · MySQL · Redis/Horizon · Workflow Engine · Governed Agent Runtime · Arabic RTL
hero.disclosure: Engineering capability showcase · seeded demonstration data
hero.shotAlt: CRMA dashboard with pipeline value, open deals, tasks due today and recent activity, on seeded demonstration data.
hero.centerAlt: AI Action Center listing pending AI proposals, each with a risk level and approve or reject controls.
hero.positioning: Built as an engineering capability showcase for modern CRM, workflow automation and governed AI systems. Every screen shows the running application on seeded demonstration data.

os.title: Sales operations in one place
os.lede: Contacts, leads, tasks, deals, the pipeline and reporting share one data model and one permission model, so a change in one module is visible in the others.

modules.name: Dashboard
modules.desc: Pipeline value, open deals, today's tasks and recent activity for the signed-in team.
modules.alt: CRMA dashboard with pipeline metrics, tasks and an activity feed.

modules.name: Contacts
modules.desc: People and companies with owners, tags and the full activity history behind every record.
modules.alt: Contacts list with names, companies, owners and tags.

modules.name: Leads
modules.desc: Inbound and captured leads with status, source and a rule-based score that explains itself.
modules.alt: Leads table with status, source and score columns.

modules.name: Tasks
modules.desc: Follow-ups with owners and due dates; overdue work is counted per owner.
modules.alt: Task list grouped by due date with owners and priorities.

modules.name: Deals
modules.desc: One deal workspace: stage, value, computed health signals and the stage history.
modules.alt: Deal workspace with stage, value, health signals labelled computed from CRM data, and stage history.

modules.name: Pipeline
modules.desc: A board of open deals by stage, with value per column.
modules.alt: Kanban pipeline with deal cards across stages and value totals per stage.

modules.name: Reports
modules.desc: Saved reports over the same tenant-scoped data the team works in.
modules.alt: Reports screen with saved report definitions and charts.

flow.title: From first contact to measured result
flow.lede: Every record follows one path. Automation and AI sit inside it; neither can skip the step where a person decides.
flow.label: The CRMA operating flow

steps.name: Capture
steps.desc: Forms, imports, signed webhooks and manual entry create leads and contacts.

steps.name: Qualify
steps.desc: Rule-based lead scoring with a per-rule explanation; owners assigned.

steps.name: Automate
steps.desc: Workflows react to record, email, form, schedule and webhook events.

steps.name: Sell
steps.desc: Deals move through pipeline stages; every stage change is recorded.

steps.name: Assist
steps.desc: Agents read CRM context and draft proposals — they never write directly.

steps.name: Approve
steps.desc: A person reviews the proposed change, its risk and its evidence.

steps.name: Measure
steps.desc: Reports, deal health and the audit log read the resulting state.

flow.note: Approval is a step in the flow, not an optional setting: governed actions cannot execute without a decision.

logic.title: Business state is computed from CRM data, not guessed by the model.
logic.lede: Scores, health and pipeline review come from fixed, testable rules over stored records. The language model may explain a number; it never produces one.
logic.pipelineAlt: Deal pipeline board with stage columns and value totals.
logic.dealAlt: Deal workspace showing health signals labelled 'Computed from CRM data, not by AI' and the deal's stage history.

items.name: Pipeline stages
items.desc: Configured stages per organization; deals carry a stage and a status.

items.name: Deal health
items.desc: A deterministic signal calculator scores each deal from activity, age and stage — AI may explain it but never produces it.

items.name: Pipeline review
items.desc: Pipeline intelligence summarises stalled and at-risk deals from the same rules, with thresholds held in configuration.

items.name: Lead scoring
items.desc: Priority, status, 30-day engagement, recency, contact completeness and value, each with its own rule and points, capped at 100.

items.name: Stage history
items.desc: Every stage change is written to its own table, so time-in-stage is measured, not estimated.

items.name: Tasks & follow-up
items.desc: Due and overdue work is counted per owner for the daily brief and the hourly proactive scan.

workflow.title: Automation you can read before it runs
workflow.lede: Workflows are drawn as graphs, synced to executable triggers and actions, and validated before they can be activated.

triad.name: Trigger
triad.desc: Record created or updated, email opened, clicked or replied, form submitted, cron schedule, signed inbound webhook.

triad.name: Condition
triad.desc: A typed expression language evaluates conditions — no eval() — with an audit command for existing workflows.

triad.name: Action
triad.desc: Controlled actions on CRM records, waits and delays, resumed by a scheduler every minute.

workflow.shotAlt: Visual workflow builder with a trigger node connected to condition and action nodes.

items.name: Graph-defined
items.desc: The visual graph is the source; trigger and action rows are synced from it.

items.name: Validated activation
items.desc: A workflow with errors cannot be switched on; the errors are returned to the builder.

items.name: Waits
items.desc: Wait and delay steps park a run; a scheduled job resumes due runs every minute.

items.name: Event-driven
items.desc: Record, email, form, schedule and webhook events start runs on queued workers.

ai.lede: Agents work inside CRM context with a tool allowlist per profile. Anything that changes data becomes a proposal: the stored current state, the proposed state, a reason, evidence and a risk class — waiting for a person.

chain.name: CRM context
chain.desc: Records the user can already see, scoped to their organization.

chain.name: Agent runtime
chain.desc: One of 14 agent profiles, each with its own tool allowlist.

chain.name: Tool
chain.desc: Read tools answer directly; write tools can only propose.

chain.name: Proposal
chain.desc: Stored with reason and evidence; expires after 72 hours by default.

chain.name: Field-level diff
chain.desc: Current and proposed values, side by side.

chain.name: Risk
chain.desc: One of five risk classes decides how it may be approved.

chain.name: Human approval
chain.desc: Approve, reject — or edit an email or WhatsApp draft, which is validated again.

chain.name: Controlled execution
chain.desc: Executed by the action handler, written to the audit log.

chain.name: Resume
chain.desc: The same agent run continues with the outcome.

risks.name: LOW_WRITE
risks.desc: Small internal writes. May be approved in bulk.

risks.name: MEDIUM_WRITE
risks.desc: Record changes. May be approved in bulk.

risks.name: HIGH_EXTERNAL
risks.desc: Leaves the system — email, WhatsApp. Never in bulk.

risks.name: CRITICAL
risks.desc: Reviewed one at a time. Never in bulk.

ai.shotAlt: Copilot chat where the agent proposes moving a deal from Qualification to Proposal, with a field-by-field before and after and Approve and Reject buttons.

diff.caption: Stored state of the proposed stage change
diff.note: Recreated from the proposal shown above. The proposal stores the before and after state; the reviewer sees both before anything changes.

points.name: Eight governed action types
points.desc: Create task, add note, update record, change deal stage, assign lead, draft workflow, send email, send WhatsApp.

points.name: Same-run resume
points.desc: A run pauses while waiting for a decision and resumes the same run afterwards — covered by runtime tests.

points.name: Edited drafts are revalidated
points.desc: A reviewer can edit an outbound email or WhatsApp draft; the edit is a new revision and is checked again.

points.name: Everything is audited
points.desc: Proposed, revised, rejected and executed events are written to the audit log.

ai.disclosure: The copilot turns on these screens were recorded with the deterministic test driver, so the tool sequence is repeatable.

knowledge.title: Answers grounded in the organization's own documents
knowledge.lede: Hybrid retrieval: keyword ranking and vector similarity, fused into one result list, with an evaluation command that fails when quality drops.

flow.name: Ingest
flow.desc: Text, file or URL; URLs fetched through the SSRF-safe fetcher.

flow.name: Fusion
flow.desc: Reciprocal rank fusion merges both lists.

flow.name: Evaluate
flow.desc: kb:eval reports recall@k and MRR against thresholds.

knowledge.shotAlt: Knowledge base screen with Text, File and URL tabs, an Index Document button and an Ask box.

points.name: Fusion ranking
points.desc: BM25 plus vector similarity, merged with reciprocal rank fusion.

points.name: Sized for a team's knowledge
points.desc: Vector similarity is computed in the application over a bounded set of recent chunks.

points.name: Measured, not assumed
points.desc: Retrieval quality has a command and thresholds, so a regression fails loudly.

arch.title: Three tiers, one tenant boundary
arch.lede: Recreated from the codebase: what talks to the application, what runs inside it, and what it depends on.

nodes.name: Tenant boundary
nodes.desc: Organization global scope, RBAC per organization, 49 policies.

nodes.name: CRM domain
nodes.desc: Contacts, leads, deals, tasks, pipeline, reports.

nodes.name: Redis · Horizon
nodes.desc: Queues for email, AI agents, webhooks, WhatsApp, imports.

nodes.name: Scheduler
nodes.desc: Workflow resume each minute, proposal expiry, hourly scan.

nodes.name: Reverb
nodes.desc: WebSocket server in the compose stack.

arch.deploy: Docker Compose: app · nginx · mysql · redis · horizon · scheduler · reverb. Release script with atomic symlink swap, health check and rollback.

security.title: Specific controls, each in code and tests
security.lede: No blanket claims. These are the mechanisms the repository implements.

items.name: Tenant isolation
items.desc: A global organization scope on tenant models, cross-tenant validation rules, and dedicated tenancy tests.

items.name: Per-organization RBAC
items.desc: Roles and permissions keyed to the organization, with API/UI policy parity tests.

items.name: Two-factor and sessions
items.desc: TOTP two-factor, session list and revoke, IP allowlist, rate limiting.

items.name: SCIM provisioning
items.desc: SCIM endpoints with their own authentication for user lifecycle.

items.name: SSRF-safe fetching
items.desc: Public-IP validation, a pinned connection and re-validation on every redirect, with a body size cap.

items.name: Idempotency and headers
items.desc: Idempotency keys on writes and a security-headers middleware.

items.name: AI tool allowlists
items.desc: Each agent profile can only call the tools it lists.

items.name: Audit trail
items.desc: AI proposals, revisions, rejections and executions are written to the audit log.

security.shotAlt: Roles and permissions matrix with permission toggles per role.

integrations.title: What is built, and what is a connector

tiers.title: Implemented
tiers.note: In the codebase, with tests or verification logic

items.name: MCP server
items.desc: OAuth 2.1 with PKCE S256, hashed audience-bound tokens, rotating refresh tokens with reuse detection; scopes crm:read and crm:propose. MCP writes become proposals.

items.name: External MCP client
items.desc: HTTPS only and SSRF-validated. An admin approves each read-only tool; approval is revoked if the tool changes.

items.name: Signed webhooks
items.desc: Twilio signature validation, Stripe event construction, Meta lead HMAC verification, inbound workflow hooks.

items.name: Model router
items.desc: Anthropic, OpenAI and OpenAI-compatible endpoints (including a local Ollama), bring-your-own-key credentials encrypted at rest, usage recorded per call.

items.name: Google Workspace
items.desc: OAuth connection; reads profile and Gmail message list.

items.name: Slack · n8n
items.desc: OAuth or token connections through the same connector catalog.

integrations.shotAlt: Connector settings listing Google Workspace, Slack and n8n, each disconnected with a connect button.
